content:
Quick answer: A flare is a worsening of symptoms, but new severe joint pain or swelling should not automatically be assumed to be an arthritis flare. The approach depends on the type of arthritis and your treatment plan.

Recognise your usual pattern

Note which joints are affected, stiffness, swelling, fatigue and any changes from your usual symptoms. Follow an existing flare plan agreed with your rheumatology or primary care team.

Adjust daily activities

Reduce demanding tasks briefly while keeping comfortable gentle movement where possible. Heat or cold may ease symptoms for some people; protect skin and avoid extremes.

Medicines and specialist advice

Do not increase steroids, change disease-modifying medicines or start anti-inflammatory medicines without appropriate advice. Ask your team what to do if symptoms are not settling.

Red flags

A suddenly hot, swollen joint, especially with fever or feeling unwell, needs urgent assessment to exclude infection. New severe neurological symptoms or significant illness also need urgent medical attention.
